\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{पारितोषिकम्} (pāritoṣikam)}{पारितोषिकम् (pāritoṣikam)}]{\sk{पारितोषिकम्} (pāritoṣikam) — a prize}

\label{lesson:SA-C194-paritosikam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for an item, then the Sanskrit for a tool.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{पारितोषिकम्}}
\textbf{\sk{पारितोषिकम्}} — \emph{pāritoṣikam} — \textquotedblleft{}a prize\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pāritoṣika} comes from \emph{paritoṣa}, \textquotedblleft{}delight, satisfaction\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{pari-} and the root √tuṣ, \textquotedblleft{}to be pleased\textquotedblright{} (MW). It first meant \textquotedblleft{}gratifying\textquotedblright{}, and then \textquotedblleft{}a reward\textquotedblright{}, the thing that pleases.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{निमन्त्रणम्} (nimantraṇam)}{निमन्त्रणम् (nimantraṇam)}]{\sk{निमन्त्रणम्} (nimantraṇam) — an invitation}

\label{lesson:SA-C194-nimantranam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a tool, then the Sanskrit for a prize.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{निमन्त्रणम्}}
\textbf{\sk{निमन्त्रणम्}} — \emph{nimantraṇam} — \textquotedblleft{}an invitation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nimantraṇa} is built on \emph{ni-} and \emph{mantrayate}, \textquotedblleft{}speaks, takes counsel\textquotedblright{}, a verb MW makes from \emph{mantra}, which is built on the root √man, \textquotedblleft{}to think\textquotedblright{}. MW glosses it \textquotedblleft{}invitation, a summons\textquotedblright{}, and Hindi took it over as \emph{nimantraṇ}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{सभा} (sabhā)}{सभा (sabhā)}]{\sk{सभा} (sabhā) — an assembly, a meeting}

\label{lesson:SA-C194-sabha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a prize, then the Sanskrit for an invitation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{सभा}}
\textbf{\sk{सभा}} — \emph{sabhā} — \textquotedblleft{}an assembly, a meeting\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sabhā} is of unknown derivation, MW says, though probably connected with \emph{sa-}, \textquotedblleft{}together\textquotedblright{}. MW compares Gothic \emph{sibja}, \textquotedblleft{}kinship\textquotedblright{}, and English \emph{gossip}, which MW also cites in its older form \emph{god-sib}. It is a Rigvedic word for an assembly or hall (CDIAL 13167).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{गोष्ठी} (goṣṭhī)}{गोष्ठी (goṣṭhī)}]{\sk{गोष्ठी} (goṣṭhī) — a discussion group}

\label{lesson:SA-C194-gosthi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for an invitation, then the Sanskrit for an assembly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{गोष्ठी}}
\textbf{\sk{गोष्ठी}} — \emph{goṣṭhī} — \textquotedblleft{}a discussion group\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{goṣṭhī} comes from \emph{goṣṭha}, a cow-pen, built on \emph{go}, \textquotedblleft{}cow\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{stha}, \textquotedblleft{}standing\textquotedblright{} (MW). The cow-pen became a meeting place, then an assembly, then a talk (CDIAL 4339). Marathi \emph{goṭh} now means \textquotedblleft{}a tale\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{मेलकः} (melakaḥ)}{मेलकः (melakaḥ)}]{\sk{मेलकः} (melakaḥ) — a fair, a gathering}

\label{lesson:SA-C194-melakah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for an assembly, then the Sanskrit for a discussion group.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{मेलकः}}
\textbf{\sk{मेलकः}} — \emph{melakaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a fair, a gathering\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{melaka} is \emph{mela}, \textquotedblleft{}meeting\textquotedblright{}, built on the root √mil, \textquotedblleft{}to meet\textquotedblright{} (MW), with the suffix \emph{-ka}. It lives on as Hindi \emph{melā}, \textquotedblleft{}fair\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10331).
\end{cousinweb}
